name: Earth at the June solstice
$comment:
A PINNED-EPOCH Earth: identical to `earth` in every way except that it names WHEN it is set, so a rig renders the same instant every run. Created 2026-08-24 because nothing could be verified in a picture otherwise. Two shots of the same build differed by 3.95% while a real change measured 1.61% — the scene ran on the wall clock, so the sun moved between runs and swamped everything. Any visual claim about light, season, shadow or colour needs a world like this to be checkable at all.

The epoch is 1718916660 = 2024-06-20 20:51 UTC, the June solstice, and it is NOT a number chosen here: `orbit.rs`'s own test fixtures already pin it as the solstice with the sun over the Tropic of Cancer (declination +23.44 deg). Reusing a verified fixture rather than inventing one means the date itself cannot be quietly wrong.

Why the solstice: it is the extreme of the axial tilt, so it is where a tilted Earth looks most different from an upright one — the terminator leans hardest and the poles are most asymmetrically lit. `time.rotation` stays false so the only thing pinned is the season, not the hour.
